import { useMemo } from 'react'

/**
 * Operating P&L calculations — full-business profitability with overhead absorption.
 *
 * Core formula (aligned with Unit Economics):
 *   Total Payout  = FK bank_settlement_projected      (cash FK actually wires us)
 *   Total Cost    = casper_breakeven × net_units      (our full cost, already includes misc/overhead allocation)
 *   Net Profit    = Total Payout − Total Cost
 *   Net Margin %  = Net Profit / Total Cost × 100     (return on cost — same anchor as Unit Economics)
 *
 * Absorption variance:
 *   We allocate overhead (rent/electricity/manpower) via `misc_total` per unit in pricing.
 *   If target_monthly_units = 700 and we deliver only 356, we under-recover fixed costs.
 *   Under-absorbed = (target − actual) × misc_per_unit
 *   misc_per_unit is the weighted average of casper_misc_total across delivered SKUs.
 *
 * Status codes for each matched SKU (cleaned up):
 *   'profit'     — Net Payout / unit > breakeven           (selling above cost AND has positive profit)
 *   'thin'       — Net Payout / unit ≥ breakeven but margin < target%   (above cost, below profit goal)
 *                  [reserved — currently same as profit unless target % is enforced]
 *   'loss'       — Net Payout / unit < breakeven           (selling below cost — unit-level loss)
 */
export function useOperatingPnlData(report) {
  return useMemo(() => {
    if (!report?.sku_rows) return emptyResult()

    const rows          = report.sku_rows
    const matchedRows   = rows.filter(r => r.is_matched && r.casper_breakeven != null)
    const unmatchedRows = rows.filter(r => !r.is_matched)

    // Per-SKU calculations
    const enriched = matchedRows.map(r => {
      const payout      = r.bank_settlement_projected || 0
      const netUnits    = r.net_units || 0
      const grossUnits  = r.gross_units || 0
      const breakeven   = r.casper_breakeven || 0
      const breakevenG  = r.casper_breakeven_gst || 0

      const payoutPerU  = netUnits > 0 ? payout / netUnits : 0
      const totalCost   = breakeven * netUnits
      const totalCostG  = breakevenG * netUnits
      const profit      = payout - totalCost
      const profitU     = netUnits > 0 ? profit / netUnits : 0
      // Return-on-cost margin — same anchor as Unit Economics view
      const marginPct   = totalCost > 0 ? (profit / totalCost) * 100 : null
      const returnRate  = grossUnits > 0 ? ((grossUnits - netUnits) / grossUnits) * 100 : 0

      // Status: 'loss' if selling below cost, else 'profit'
      const status = (payoutPerU < breakeven || payoutPerU < 0) ? 'loss' : 'profit'

      return {
        ...r,
        true_payout:      payout,
        true_total_cost:  totalCost,
        true_total_cost_gst: totalCostG,
        true_profit:      profit,
        true_profit_u:    profitU,
        true_margin_pct:  marginPct,
        true_bs_per_u:    payoutPerU,
        true_return_pct:  returnRate,
        true_status:      status,
      }
    })

    // Totals — uniform naming across Unit Economics + Operating P&L
    const totalPayout    = enriched.reduce((s, r) => s + r.true_payout, 0)
    const totalCost      = enriched.reduce((s, r) => s + r.true_total_cost, 0)
    const totalCostGst   = enriched.reduce((s, r) => s + r.true_total_cost_gst, 0)
    const totalNetUnits  = enriched.reduce((s, r) => s + (r.net_units || 0), 0)
    // Net Profit = Payout − Cost (no overhead adjustment yet) — same definition as Unit Economics
    const netProfit      = totalPayout - totalCost
    const netMargin      = totalCost > 0 ? (netProfit / totalCost) * 100 : null
    // After-GST counterparts
    const netProfitGst   = totalPayout - totalCostGst
    const netMarginGst   = totalCostGst > 0 ? (netProfitGst / totalCostGst) * 100 : null

    // Absorption (volume variance against target)
    const targetUnits      = report.target_monthly_units || 0
    // Weighted average misc per unit across delivered SKUs (from live pricing)
    const miscWeighted = enriched.reduce((s, r) => s + (r.casper_misc_total || 0) * (r.net_units || 0), 0)
    const miscPerUnit      = totalNetUnits > 0 ? miscWeighted / totalNetUnits : 0
    const targetAbsorption = targetUnits * miscPerUnit
    const actualAbsorption = totalNetUnits * miscPerUnit
    const absorptionGap    = targetAbsorption - actualAbsorption   // positive = under-absorbed
    const volumePct        = targetUnits > 0 ? (totalNetUnits / targetUnits) * 100 : null

    // "Final" line items = Net Profit minus un-recovered overhead drag
    // (Net Profit already accounts for miscPerUnit × netUnits via breakeven, so the
    //  drag is only the overhead we FAILED to recover on the MISSING units)
    const overheadDrag = Math.max(0, absorptionGap)
    const finalProfit  = netProfit - overheadDrag
    const finalMargin  = totalCost > 0 ? (finalProfit / totalCost) * 100 : null

    // Pattern groupings — "Kill List" (industry term) = SKUs selling below cost
    const killList = enriched
      .filter(r => r.true_status === 'loss')
      .sort((a, b) => a.true_profit_u - b.true_profit_u)

    const returnLeakage = enriched
      .filter(r => r.true_return_pct >= 30)
      .sort((a, b) => b.true_return_pct - a.true_return_pct)

    const dataGap = unmatchedRows
      .slice()
      .sort((a, b) => (b.gross_units || 0) - (a.gross_units || 0))

    return {
      rows: enriched,
      totals: {
        payout:           totalPayout,
        total_cost:       totalCost,
        total_cost_gst:   totalCostGst,
        net_profit:       netProfit,         // Payout − Cost (matches Unit Economics)
        net_margin:       netMargin,         // Net Profit / Cost × 100
        net_profit_gst:   netProfitGst,
        net_margin_gst:   netMarginGst,      // Net Profit (GST) / Cost (GST) × 100
        overhead_drag:    overheadDrag,
        final_profit:     finalProfit,       // Net Profit − Overhead Drag (real bottom line)
        final_margin:     finalMargin,
        total_units:      totalNetUnits,     // renamed from "Net Units"
        misc_per_unit:    miscPerUnit,
        target_units:     targetUnits,
        target_absorp:    targetAbsorption,
        actual_absorp:    actualAbsorption,
        absorption_gap:   absorptionGap,
        volume_pct:       volumePct,
        kill_count:       killList.length,
        gap_count:        dataGap.length,
      },
      killList,
      returnLeakage,
      dataGap,
    }
  }, [report])
}

function emptyResult() {
  return {
    rows: [],
    totals: {
      payout: 0, total_cost: 0, total_cost_gst: 0,
      net_profit: 0, net_margin: null, net_profit_gst: 0, net_margin_gst: null,
      overhead_drag: 0, final_profit: 0, final_margin: null,
      total_units: 0, misc_per_unit: 0,
      target_units: 0, target_absorp: 0, actual_absorp: 0,
      absorption_gap: 0, volume_pct: null, kill_count: 0, gap_count: 0,
    },
    killList: [],
    returnLeakage: [],
    dataGap: [],
  }
}

The Dashboard is your starting view after login. It rolls up the data from SKUs, Pricing, and uploaded P&L reports into a single summary so you can answer in 5 seconds: "How is the business doing this month?"

Every section is driven by your own live data, scoped to the active company. A brand-new company starts empty and fills in as you add SKUs, pricing, and upload P&L reports.
  • Metrics ribbon — sell-through, customer-return, RTO, fraud-signal rate, settlement rate, avg net margin, and top fraud signals.

  • Settlement reconciliation — settled vs. expected payout and where cash is leaking.
  • Fraud action pipeline — flagged actors and recommended actions.
  • Reports — order funnel, fee waterfall, and return-reason drill-down.

The Dashboard is a launchpad. Common next steps:

  • Spotting a dip in margin? → Open P&L → Operating P&L to find the cause.
  • Adding a new product? → SKUs → Manage SKUs.
  • Uploading this month's settlement? → P&L → Flipkart (or other platform).

The P&L module compares the actual settlement Flipkart paid you against the target prices you set in the SKUs page — at the per-SKU level AND at the business level.

It answers two distinct questions:

  • Profit & Loss tab — "Which SKUs made or lost money this month?"
  • Operating P&L tab — "Did the entire business make money this month, after fixed overhead?"
Upload a Flipkart settlement Excel once per month. The system parses it, matches each line to your Casper SKU master, and computes the variance.

1. Flipkart Report — raw data view of the uploaded Excel.

2. Profit & Loss — per-SKU spreadsheet. 16 columns grouped into: Sold · Target · Actual · Variance / Bottom Line. Click 🔗 next to any SKU to jump to its master record.

3. Operating P&L — executive dashboard with verdict banner, KPI strip, and action cards (Kill List, Return Leakage, Data Gap, Volume Absorption). NO per-SKU table — that's the P&L tab's job.

4. Insights — charts: variance waterfall, margin distribution, fee breakdown.

Flipkart's settlement file shows a "Net Margins %" column that often looks positive even on losing SKUs. That's because FK computes: 

FK Net Margin %  =  Net Earnings ÷ Accounted Net Sales

They don't know your cost — they only know their sale and their deductions. A SKU can show "+37% margin" in FK's report and still be a real loss for you, because the ₹627 they paid is below your ₹1,807 cost.

When you see different margin numbers in Flipkart's report vs Casper, both are correct — they answer different questions. Casper anchors on YOUR cost; FK anchors on THEIR revenue.

Each P&L row carries a status:

  • 🟢 Profit — Net Payout per unit ≥ Breakeven
  • 🔴 Loss — Net Payout per unit < Breakeven (selling below cost)

Pattern cards in Operating P&L surface SKUs needing attention: Kill List (below cost), Return Leakage (return rate > 30%), Data Gap (FK SKU not in master).

  • Negative Net Payout — happens when returns + reverse-ship exceed sales (e.g., SHJ-JS-VRI-N64-BLUE). Math handles this correctly; the SKU lands in the Kill List.
  • Unmatched SKUs — FK SKU names not in your Casper master are excluded from cost/profit calculations (would be misleading to half-compute). Shown in the "Data Gap" pattern card.
  • Zero net units — SKUs where everything was returned/cancelled. Per-unit metrics show "—".
  • Stale pricing — P&L pulls breakeven live from sku_pricing. Edit pricing on SKUs page → refresh report → numbers update.

The SKUs page is your source of truth for pricing. Each row is one product. You enter your real-world costs (raw price, packaging, logistics, etc.) and the system computes everything downstream — breakeven, target price, per-platform listing prices.

Edits here flow live into the Pricing page, the P&L module, and the Operating P&L dashboard. There is no separate "save and recalculate" step — change a cost, the breakeven updates.

Think of it as a spreadsheet with brains. Each row has 18 columns grouped into Unit Economics → Profitability → Bank Settlement → Per-Platform Listing.

Cost components (1–5) — your real spend per unit:

  • Price — raw product cost only (vendor invoice)
  • Package — box + label + tape + other packing per unit
  • Logistics — vendor/factory → warehouse (outbound is platform's job)
  • Addons — free gifts, extras bundled with each unit
  • Misc — overhead per unit (rent ÷ target units, etc.)

Reserves (6–9) — money you set aside per unit for returns and damage:

  • CR % / CR ₹ — bidirectional. Customer Return target ceiling. ₹ = % × platform reverse-shipping cost.
  • Damage % / Damage ₹ — bidirectional. Anchored on Price. Damaged unit = full write-off.

Profitability (10–13) — the floor and the goal:

  • Breakeven — cost recovery floor (cost + reserves)
  • Breakeven (GST) — breakeven × (1 + GST%)
  • Profit % / Profit ₹ — bidirectional. Target margin on top of breakeven.

Bank Settlement (14–15) — what you want to receive:

  • Target Pre-GST — breakeven + profit
  • Target Post-GST — Target Pre-GST + GST

Per-platform tail (16–18) — varies by platform:

  • AD %/₹ — advertising/acquisition cost per unit (varies by platform)
  • Tier — platform commission. Dual-mode: % or ₹.
  • BS per Platform — listing price (MRP) calculated for that platform
 Breakeven is the floor — the price below which you lose money on this SKU. It bakes in your costs PLUS the reserves you keep for returns and damage. Above this number = profit. Below = loss. } example={{ title: 'Worked example — jewellery SKU', inputs: [ { label: 'Price', value: '₹63' }, { label: 'Package', value: '₹7' }, { label: 'Logistics', value: '₹10' }, { label: 'Addons', value: '₹6' }, { label: 'Misc (overhead/unit)', value: '₹12' }, { label: 'CR Reserve (20% × ₹168)', value: '₹33.60' }, { label: 'Damage Reserve (8% × ₹63)', value: '₹5.04' }, ], breakdown: 'Breakeven = 63 + 7 + 10 + 6 + 12 + 33.60 + 5.04 = ₹136.64', output: { label: 'Breakeven', value: '₹136.64', valueClass: '' }, }} variants={[ { title: 'Adding profit + GST → Target Post-GST (final listing target)', formula: `Target Pre-GST = Breakeven + (Breakeven × Profit %) Target Post-GST = Target Pre-GST × (1 + GST %)`, explanation: 'Profit is markup on top of breakeven. CR, Damage, and Profit each have a % and a ₹ field that stay in sync. Type 20 in the % field — the ₹ field auto-fills. Type ₹34 in the ₹ field — the % back-computes. The math is the same; only the unit you enter changes.

Anchors (the "what is this a percentage OF?"):

  • CR ₹ = CR % × Platform's reverse-shipping cost (e.g., Flipkart = ₹168)
  • Damage ₹ = Damage % × Price
  • Profit ₹ = Profit % × Breakeven (no GST)

New SKUs auto-fill CR %, Damage %, and Profit % from their category's defaults. For example, if "Jewellery Set" is set to CR=20% / Dmg=15% / Profit=20%, creating a new SKU in that category gets those values pre-filled.

You can still override any field per SKU. The cascade only fills empty fields — never overrides what you typed.

Manage category defaults: SKUs page → category dropdown → Manage Categories →.

Each row has a section per active platform showing:

  • AD %/₹ — your advertising cost per unit on that platform. Use the ↑ Upload Ad button in the platform header to import a CSV/XLSX of campaign spend and auto-compute per-SKU AD/unit.
  • Tier — dropdown of named commission tiers for that platform (e.g., Standard / Premium). Each tier carries either a fixed ₹ fee or a % of base BS. Click "+ Add tier…" in the dropdown to create a new tier without leaving this page.
  • BS per Platform — the listing price (MRP) Casper recommends so that, after the platform's deductions, you still hit your Target Pre-GST.
  • Misc is a per-unit average — based on overhead ÷ target net delivered units/month. Reviewed quarterly.
  • CR reserve under-funds reality when actual CR % exceeds your target. The "Return Leakage" pattern card in Operating P&L flags SKUs where actual > 30%.
  • Damage anchors on Price only (not full landed cost). Slightly under-reserves the true write-off cost; parked for revisit in ideas_parking.md.
  • GST is platform-pass-through — collected on sale, remitted to government. Doesn't reduce your bank settlement but is accounted in Target Post-GST.

import IntroPage, { IntroSection, TechSection, Callout } from '../../components/IntroPage' export default function SettingsIntro() { return (

Settings is where you manage the platform configuration that drives all pricing calculations across the app. Every number you enter here flows into the SKUs page breakeven formula and the P&L computations.

Key things you configure here:

  • Platforms — Flipkart, Meesho, Snapdeal, Amazon, etc.
  • Reverse-shipping cost per platform — the fee charged per return
  • Commission tiers per platform — named tiers with a fixed ₹ or % fee
  • Default AD % per platform — advertising cost assumption
Changing a platform's reverse-shipping cost affects the CR Reserve on every SKU linked to that platform. Review affected SKUs after any change.

Each platform record stores:

  • Name — Flipkart, Meesho, Snapdeal, Amazon, etc.
  • Reverse-ship cost (CR Charge) — what the platform charges you when a customer returns an item. Currently: Flipkart = ₹168. Used as the anchor for CR Reserve in every SKU: CR ₹ = CR % × reverse_ship_cost.
  • Default AD % — platform-wide advertising default. Snapdeal = 10%. Can be overridden per SKU via ad-report upload on the SKUs page.

Each platform has one or more named commission tiers — for example:

  • Standard — ₹71.5 flat fee per order (Flipkart example)
  • Premium — 5% of base bank settlement

Each tier can be set as a fixed ₹ amount OR a % of MRP. When editing, switch the mode dropdown between ₹ and %.

On the SKUs page, each (SKU, platform) pair picks one of these tiers. The listing price is back-calculated so that after the tier deduction you still hit your Target Post-GST.

You can also add a tier directly from the SKUs page tier dropdown — click "+ Add tier…" without navigating here.

The chain from Settings → SKU price:

  1. Settings: reverse_ship_cost = ₹168 for Flipkart
  2. SKUs page: CR % = 20% → CR Reserve = 20% × 168 = ₹33.60/unit
  3. Breakeven includes CR Reserve → rises by ₹33.60
  4. Target Post-GST rises accordingly → Listing Price rises

If Flipkart raises their reverse-ship fee from ₹168 → ₹185, update it here once — all 50 SKUs recalculate automatically.

The Vendors page manages your supplier list — the businesses or individuals you buy products from. Each vendor has a name and a short code (e.g., SHJ) that prefixes your SKU IDs so you always know the source at a glance.

A vendor is linked to SKUs — each SKU belongs to one vendor. The count on each vendor card shows how many SKUs are sourced from that supplier.

  • SKU: SHJ-JS-VRI-N65-WHITE — prefix tells you it came from Shringar House

This makes it easy to sort, filter, and group SKUs by supplier in bulk exports and reports.
